record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Is PCP decidable for unique equality continuation instances?

evidence.quote: Is PCP decidable for unique equality continuation instances?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An instance of the Post Correspondence Problem (PCP) over a finite alphabet $A$ is a pair of morphisms $g, h : B^* \to A^*$, where $B$ is a finite set of indices. A solution is a nonempty word $w \in B^+$ with $g(w) = h(w)$; the PCP asks, given $(g,h)$, whether such a $w$ exists.

For an instance $(g,h)$ and words $u, v \in A^*$, say that a word $w \in B^*$ is an equality continuation from $(u,v)$ if $u\,g(w) = v\,h(w)$. The instance $(g,h)$ is said to have unique equality continuations if for every pair $(u,v) \in A^* \times A^*$ that is reachable as a prefix pair during the reading of some attempted matching (equivalently, for every $(u,v)$ such that there exists at least one $w \in B^*$ with $u\,g(w) = v\,h(w)$), there is at most one letter $b \in B$ that can extend $(u,v)$ towards equality, in the sense that $u\,g(b)$ is a prefix of $v\,h(b)$ or vice versa.

Question: Is the Post Correspondence Problem decidable when restricted to instances $(g,h)$ that have unique equality continuations? That is, does there exist an algorithm which, given any such instance, decides whether it admits a solution $w \in B^+$ with $g(w) = h(w)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The corresponding ω-PCP (infinite-solution) version for unique continuation instances is known to be decidable (Halava, Harju, Karhumäki, Latteux). However, decidability of the (finite) PCP for unique equality continuation instances does not appear in the literature as resolved; it is listed among open questions in surveys on PCP variants and no decidability or undecidability proof was located.

status_evidence.title: Extension of the decidability of the marked PCP to instances with unique blocks
status_evidence.snippet: It is decidable whether an instance satisfying the uniqueness condition for continuations has an infinite solution.
status_evidence.claim: The ω-PCP version for unique continuation instances is decidable, but the finite-solution version is not addressed there.

status_evidence.title: Decidable Instances of the Post Correspondence Problem (Ackerman)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of decidable subclasses of PCP including marked, unique-block, and unique continuation instances.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability of PCP restricted to unique equality continuation instances is not established in surveys of decidable PCP subclasses.
